All Headings.title: <h1> to <h6> — The Content Hierarchy Blueprint
All Headings.history:
The foundational roadmap that structures your website's topics for readers and search bots.

Heading tags range from <h1> (most important) to <h6> (least important). They are not meant to make text look big or bold—that is CSS's job. Instead, they act as the index of your page, mapping out sections so web crawlers and screen readers can instantly digest the logical architecture of your content layout.
All Headings.tip: The Strict SEO Golden Rule: Never use more than one <h1> tag on a single webpage! Think of your <h1> as the book title, and <h2> through <h6> as chapters and sub-sections. Breaking this order confuses Google's indexing spiders and hurts your ranking.

em.title: <em> — The Voice Stress & Emphasis Tag
em.history:
Tells browsers, screen readers, and search engines where to put the acoustic weight in a sentence.

The <em> element is a semantic formatting tag used to emphasize words. While it physically renders text in italics by default, its true purpose is programmatic. It visually changes the tone of the sentence, changing how a text-to-speech screen reader verbally pronounces the word to a visually impaired user.
em.tip: The Semantics Rule (em vs. i): Never use <em> just to make text look pretty and slanted—use CSS font-style: italic; or the <i> tag for that! Use <em> only when changing the word's stress actually changes the meaning of the spoken sentence.

h2.title: <h2> Subheading Tag
h2.history:
Used for subheadings. Smaller than h1.

Subheadings are used to organize content into sections.
h2.tip: The <h2> tag is used for subheadings, which are smaller than the main heading (<h1>) but still represent a section of the content.

p.title: Paragraph Tag
p.history:
Used to write paragraphs of text.

Paragraphs are used to structure blocks of content.
p.tip: The <p> tag is used to define paragraphs of text.

br.title: Line Break Tag
br.history:
Used to insert a single line break in text content.

Line breaks are used to create new lines within a paragraph.
br.tip: The <br> tag is used to insert a line break in HTML.
br.quiz: Which tag is used to insert a line break in HTML?

i.title: <i> Italic Tag
i.history:
Used to italicize text (without emphasis).

The <i> tag is used for styling purposes only.
i.tip: The <i> tag is used to make text italic.

u.title: <u> Underline Tag
u.history:
Used to underline text.

Underlining is used for stylistic purposes.
u.tip: The <u> tag is used to underline text.

mark.title: <mark> Highlight Tag
mark.history:
Used to highlight text.

Highlighting is used to draw attention to specific parts of the content.
mark.tip: The <mark> tag is used to highlight text.

small.title: <small> Small Text Tag
small.history:
Used to show smaller text.

The <small> tag is used to decrease the size of text.
small.tip: The <small> tag is used to show small text.

sup.title: <sup> Superscript Tag
sup.history:
Used for superscript (like math powers).

The <sup> tag is used to create superscripted text.
sup.tip: The <sup> tag is used to show superscript.

sub.title: <sub> Subscript Tag
sub.history:
Used for subscript (like chemical formulas).

The <sub> tag is used to create subscripted text.
